claims.statement: Polish employers cannot admit an employee to a specified job without a current medical certificate, must issue the referral, and pay for initial, periodic and control examinations; a control examination is triggered after illness lasting more than 30 days.

Mandatory initial-exam frequency is lower than hires: an employee can be exempt after returning to the same employer within 30 days or joining another employer within 30 days when the prior certificate and referral cover equivalent conditions, except particularly dangerous work.

The employer referral must identify the examination type, job or jobs, and actual hazardous, harmful or nuisance factors with exposure levels and current measurements; the examination ends in a physician's fit/unfit certificate, not a platform eligibility decision.
Only appropriately qualified physicians may perform prophylactic examinations, and occupational-medicine professionals are statutorily independent from employers and other commissioning parties.

Initial, periodic and control examinations are performed under a written contract between the obligated employer and a registered basic occupational-medicine unit; the contract covers registration, delivery, pricing and payment and must last at least one year. The basic unit may subcontract specified diagnostics and specialist consultations and bears those costs.

Poland recorded about 5.08 million Labour-Code occupational examinations in 2024: over 2.11 million initial, 2.44 million periodic and 523 thousand control examinations. The system included 5,401 basic units, 5,516 registered physicians and about 415 thousand employer-unit contracts.

In 2024, 99.4% of prophylactic examinations ended with a positive certificate. This documents throughput but does not show referral-error rates, scheduling delay, admin time or willingness to pay an orchestration fee.

Staffing is a named, enumerable niche: 8,550 registered employment agencies operated at year-end 2024. Temporary-work agencies sent 698,081 people to assignments, but only 264,957 were employees on fixed-term employment contracts while 432,266 were non-employees on civil contracts; therefore 698,081 is not a valid mandatory-exam denominator.
The official KRAZ interface exposes a prospecting base searchable by agency name, NIP, location, legal form and service type, including temporary work.

For occupational medicine, the referring employer and the medical facility are separate data controllers, not joint controllers; the clinic cannot disclose employee medical documentation to the employer. An IT or online-booking vendor can instead be the clinic's processor when it acts on the clinic's instructions.

Occupational-medicine certificates entered the national e-health system in 2026: electronic issue is optional through 17 October 2026 and mandatory from 18 October 2026; the employee can retrieve the certificate and validity date from IKP and send the PDF to the employer.
PZU Zdrowie already offers employers a portal that automates referral handling, a named account manager, call-centre booking and examination organization in nearly 800 Polish facilities.

MedycynaPracy24.pl offers a near-direct substitute: a framework contract with no subscription or monthly minimum, payment only for performed examinations, a free referral generator, one consolidated invoice, partner facilities in 24 cities, 24-hour appointment commitments and 10-20% volume discounts.

Comarch ERP Optima 2026 already identifies workers whose periodic exam validity falls within 30 days and employees returning from uninterrupted illness longer than 30 days, absorbing two important eligibility and alert triggers inside payroll software.

A current direct clinic price list charges PLN 130 for a general prophylactic examination and certificate, PLN 110 for common specialist consultations, and roughly PLN 13-70 for listed diagnostic tests. These are retail prices, not evidence that a clinic will share margin with an intermediary.

A separate PLN 25-40 orchestration fee would need to create demonstrable faster starts or employer labour savings beyond bundled clinic portals, free referral tools and payroll alerts; mandatory medical spend alone does not establish willingness to pay this extra layer.

If tested at all, the most accessible niche is a staffing agency that itself employs many temporary workers under employment contracts and sends them to several Polish cities; the agency's actual annual Art. 229 exam count remains unknown.

No sourced evidence establishes that registered clinics will expose live appointment inventory, accept platform routing, or pay/share at least PLN 25-40 per completed examination after their existing employer discounts.

No sourced evidence establishes employer-side incremental willingness to pay, no-show and rescheduling rates, manual-support minutes, acquisition cost, clinic payout timing or a compliant cross-controller data-reuse right.

contrary_evidence: The open clinic-inventory premise is structurally constrained by mandatory employer-basic-unit contracts of at least one year. [evidence: SRC02, SRC03]
PZU Zdrowie and MedycynaPracy24.pl already bundle national or multi-city booking, referrals, support and contract administration. [evidence: SRC09, SRC10]
Comarch payroll software already finds approaching periodic exams and post-30-day-illness returns, reducing the value of a standalone rules engine. [evidence: SRC11]
National e-certificates become mandatory on 18 October 2026, commoditizing paper certificate transport and some validity tracking. [evidence: SRC08]
Existing 10-20% B2B clinic discounts are evidence of buyer savings, not of an extra commission available to a new intermediary. [evidence: SRC10, SRC12]

economics.acquisition_route: Build a 200-account Mazovia-first list from KRAZ, contact owner/COO/HR/OHS leaders with a measured faster-start offer, and win the first three agencies founder-led; add clinic and payroll referrals only after two paid reorders. Registry access is evidenced (SRC05, SRC06), but contact conversion, channel fees and CAC are unknown.
economics.capital_required_pln: Cap the pre-proof pilot at PLN 60,000-90,000: PLN 20,000 occupational-law/privacy advice and contracts, PLN 15,000 security and insurance, PLN 15,000 booking/referral MVP and messaging, PLN 10,000-20,000 clinic onboarding/manual operations, and no more than PLN 20,000 contingency. This fits the founder's own approximately PLN 100,000 only if clinics invoice employers directly; do not use parental capital or finance clinical receivables.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Use the founder snapshot definition: founder-owned business equity plus personal cash/distributions minus liabilities, excluding the home and never double-counting company retained cash. Months 0-6: spend no more than PLN 90,000, complete 200 paid exams and remain employed. Month 12 milestone: 6,000 completions x PLN 30 = PLN 180,000 revenue and PLN 132,000 contribution; still remain employed until positive contribution, repeat demand, objective traction and 12 months of personal runway are all present. Year 3 milestone: 50,000 completions, PLN 1.50m revenue, about PLN 1.10m contribution and no more than PLN 0.60m fixed costs, yielding roughly PLN 0.50m EBITDA and an illustrative 3x value of PLN 1.50m. Year 5 target: 120,000 completions, PLN 3.60m revenue, PLN 2.64m contribution and PLN 1.20m fixed costs, yielding PLN 1.44m EBITDA; at a conservative 4x multiple the business equity is PLN 5.76m and a 90% founder stake is PLN 5.18m before personal cash and liabilities. Count only actually distributed, taxed personal cash separately and assume no debt. This crosses PLN 5m around month 60 only if 120,000 events—2.4% of the 5.08m national exam market and 45% of the 264,957 temporary employees on employment contracts—are reached; that is a demanding, currently unsupported expansion beyond the initial niche.
economics.founder_time: Pilot ceiling: 25 hours/week, matching five hours/day—about 12 hours product/data, 8 hours employer and clinic sales/contracts, and 5 hours operations/legal. An authorized clinic lead owns all medical decisions. Stop on fit if manual support exceeds ten minutes per completion, urgent escalations exceed two per day, or sales requires sustained travel and high-touch relationship management.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Inference: at PLN 30 revenue, budget PLN 8 variable cost per completion (about PLN 6 for ten minutes of support at PLN 36/hour plus PLN 2 messaging, booking and payment tooling), leaving PLN 22 or 73% contribution before founder sales, legal, security and fixed payroll. Clinical charges remain between clinic and employer. Reject merchant-of-record economics unless a signed pilot proves at least 20% gross margin after clinic payment, refunds and no-shows; current sources do not prove that margin.
economics.payback: Illustrative, not evidence: an agency producing 600 paid completions per year yields PLN 13,200 annual contribution at PLN 22 each. A hard CAC cap of PLN 2,500 would repay in about 2.3 active months at 50 completions per month. Stop if the median pilot account has fewer than 250 eligible completions per year or fully loaded CAC exceeds one year of account contribution.
economics.pricing: Unvalidated test price: PLN 30 net per completed exam as a separate agency-paid orchestration fee, or a clinic-funded share of at least PLN 30 only when signed before the pilot. Do not mark up the clinical bill or assume a commission. Benchmarks: SOLMED lists PLN 130 for the basic exam/certificate plus add-ons, while MedycynaPracy24.pl advertises employer discounts of 10-20% and no subscription (SRC10, SRC12).
economics.retention_or_repeat: The legal triggers recur through hires, certificate expiries and returns after illness, and the medical-unit contract lasts at least one year (SRC01-SRC03). Frequency is weakened by initial-exam exemptions and civil-contract cohorts. Require two paid cohorts per agency within 90 days, a second paid order and active use at month six; mandatory spend alone is not retention evidence.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Privacy-minimized operational data on appointment lead time, referral correction, no-show and clinic SLA by non-medical pathway, reusable only where controller contracts expressly permit it; outcome or medical-record data are excluded from the moat claim.
fingerprint.customer: Polish staffing agencies that themselves employ at least 500 temporary workers per year under employment contracts and place them across multiple cities; exclude civil-contract-only cohorts from the initial segment.
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Founder-led outbound from the official KRAZ list, filtered by temporary-work service and geography, followed only after paid proof by referrals from registered clinics and integrations or referrals from payroll and HR vendors.
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: A non-diagnostic concierge and software layer operating inside each employer-basic-unit contract: employer-approved hazard templates, referral completeness checks, routing only to authorized contracted units or their permitted subcontractors, reminders, rescheduling and proof of certificate handoff. No medical judgment, diagnosis or medical-record access.
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The staffing agency pays a separately disclosed PLN 30 orchestration fee only after a completed examination and certificate handoff; the registered medical unit bills the clinical services directly unless a compliant alternative is proven in writing.
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A new temporary employee, qualifying job or hazard change, expiring certificate, or return after more than 30 days of illness creates an urgent need for a correct employer-signed referral, a contract-compliant appointment and a timely certificate.

founder_fit: Strong analytical and automation fit: the founder can build privacy-minimized referral checks, operational measurement and routing logic.
Warsaw location is useful for a Mazovia staffing-agency and clinic pilot, and the official KRAZ list reduces dependence on broad networking.

Low social energy and a five-hours-per-day ceiling conflict with clinic contracting, employer sales, time-sensitive rescheduling and multilingual employee support unless the pilot proves support below ten minutes per completion.
The founder's medical-student partner is not evidence of occupational-medicine licensure and cannot substitute for an authorized physician or registered basic unit.

The founder's approximately PLN 100,000 personal-capital envelope can fund a tightly capped pilot only if clinics bill employers directly; it is not enough for clinical working capital or a staffed nationwide network.
risks: {"mitigation": "Limit automation to employer-approved referral completeness and logistics; route all scope and fitness decisions to the authorized occupational physician and contractually document the boundary.", "risk": "The platform unintentionally performs or implies medical eligibility judgment."}

{"mitigation": "Obtain a written Polish occupational-law opinion and operate only within named basic units and expressly permitted subcontractors before the first employee is booked.", "risk": "Cross-clinic routing breaches the employer-basic-unit contract or unauthorized subcontracting rules."}

{"mitigation": "Keep medical records with the clinic, store only minimum referral, appointment and certificate-status fields, sign controller/processor terms, apply retention limits and prohibit cross-client reuse absent explicit legal basis.", "risk": "Sensitive medical or employment data are over-collected or reused without a lawful basis."}

{"mitigation": "Require a paid, comparative concierge pilot showing at least 20% shorter appointment lead time or one employer admin hour saved per 50 examinations, plus two reorders, before building integrations.", "risk": "Incumbents bundle the same workflow at zero incremental software price or with exam discounts."}

{"mitigation": "Keep clinics as billers, charge after completion, instrument every support minute and stop if variable contribution is below 70% or support exceeds ten minutes per completion.", "risk": "No-shows, rescheduling, multilingual support and payment operations destroy part-time fit and margin."}

{"mitigation": "Use the explicit milestones; stop if month 12 is below 6,000 completions or year 3 below 50,000 rather than extrapolating from national exam volume.", "risk": "A superficially large mandatory-spend market fails to produce the volume needed for founder wealth."}
thesis: Narrow the concept to staffing agencies that employ workers under employment contracts across several Polish cities, and test a non-clinical booking and referral-quality service inside valid employer-basic-unit contracts. Charge only a separately evidenced per-completed-exam orchestration fee; do not assume mandatory exam spend, clinic discounts or medical outcomes form an intermediary margin or moat.
title: Contract-bound occupational-medicine orchestration for high-turnover Polish staffing agencies
uncertainties: No measured denominator of Art. 229 examination events exists for agencies meeting the proposed 500-employees-per-year threshold. [evidence: SRC05]
No clinic has documented live-slot access, a commission, payment timing or permission for the proposed routing role. [evidence: SRC02, SRC10, SRC12]
No employer has documented a separate budget, paid pilot or reorder for incremental orchestration. [evidence: SRC09, SRC10, SRC11]
The compliant controller/processor/agent structure and direct access to national e-certificate data remain unresolved. [evidence: SRC07, SRC08]
No-show, support, referral-correction, appointment-delay and acquisition-cost distributions remain unmeasured.
